newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tigon soars 16 pct in continued recovery.
newsitem.headline: Tigon soars 16 pct in continued recovery.

text.p: Shares in South African electronics distributor and financial services group Tigon Ltd continued a steady recovery on Wednesday with dealers saying the stock's woes over its recent suspension seemed over.

By 1002 GMT Tigon, which came off heavily over the past two weeks following its suspension on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on May 14, was up 110 cents at 800 cents on a volume of 106,800 shares.
It was the third highest percentage gainer on the JSE.
"I think Tigon's over the bad news now. There is nothing wrong with the company, they just had to show how their earnings were made," one dealer said.
The JSE had suspended the firm's shares over the accounting of its 1996 financial results.

Tigon then later said 17.9 million rand, or 54 percent of its income for the period, was based on a fee that was not due to be received until October, prompting the JSE to lift its suspension on May 16.

"I think the market just knocked it (share) down on the news that came into the market and there just has to be a correction. I think they are just going to consolidate at these levels for a while," another dealer added.
